tasks.user_prompt: Using the checked-out query-core and its compiled bundle, compare two fresh QueryClient instances, each with retry:false and gcTime:Infinity. Seed ['q'] with 'seed', then subscribe one QueryObserver to that key with a stale queryFn returning a manually controlled pending promise. In case A the function never reads context.signal; in case B it reads and saves context.signal but does not attach listeners, reject on abort, or pass it to another API. Unsubscribe the sole observer while the promise is pending, flush microtasks, inspect data/fetchStatus and (where saved) signal.aborted, then resolve the underlying promise to 'remote' and flush settlement. What is observed at each stage, including final status and call counts, and why? Trace the signal property, observer removal, retryer cancellation and cache update paths. Use a deferred promise rather than timing races. Assume online/focused operation, no other observers, no explicit cancellation and no GC. Does merely reading the signal count as cancellation support for this implementation, even though our promise never reacts to abort?

provenance.rewrite_note: Newly authored controlled counterfactual task from pinned implementation; not represented as a real user report. Source and tests inspected; executable probe run in existing immutable Modal image.

claims.text: Reading the context.signal getter marks the signal consumed even if the user function never attaches an abort listener or passes the signal to a transport.
After the only observer unsubscribes without reading signal, the active promise continues; only future retries are cancelled. The seeded data remains while fetchStatus is fetching.
If signal was read, removing the last observer cancels with revert:true, aborts the signal and restores seeded success data with idle fetchStatus.
Resolving the user deferred promise to remote afterwards populates the unconsumed case but cannot overwrite reverted seed in the consumed case; the user promise need not itself reject or stop work.

Both cases call queryFn once; after settlement both are success/idle, with remote only in the unconsumed case and seed in the consumed case. The result is for an active seeded background fetch, not the separate paused/pending branch.

assertions.code:
import json
import subprocess
js = "const {QueryClient, QueryObserver}=require('/opt/query-core.cjs'); const assert=require('node:assert/strict'); const tick=()=>new Promise(r=>setImmediate(r));\n(async()=>{const rows=[];for(const consume of [false,true]){const c=new QueryClient({defaultOptions:{queries:{gcTime:Infinity,retry:false}}});c.setQueryData(['q'],'seed');let resolve;let signal;let calls=0;const o=new QueryObserver(c,{queryKey:['q'],queryFn:ctx=>{calls++;if(consume)signal=ctx.signal;return new Promise(r=>resolve=r)},gcTime:Infinity,retry:false});const off=o.subscribe(()=>{});const q=c.getQueryCache().find({queryKey:['q']});off();await tick();const afterUnsubscribe={data:q.state.data,fetchStatus:q.state.fetchStatus,aborted:signal?signal.aborted:null};resolve('remote');await tick();await tick();rows.push({consume,calls,afterUnsubscribe,final:{data:q.state.data,fetchStatus:q.state.fetchStatus,status:q.state.status}});c.clear();}console.log(JSON.stringify(rows));})().catch(e=>{console.error(e);process.exitCode=1});"
result = subprocess.run(["node", "-"], input=js, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=20, check=True)
actual = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert actual == [{'consume': False, 'calls': 1, 'afterUnsubscribe': {'data': 'seed', 'fetchStatus': 'fetching', 'aborted': None}, 'final': {'data': 'remote', 'fetchStatus': 'idle', 'status': 'success'}}, {'consume': True, 'calls': 1, 'afterUnsubscribe': {'data': 'seed', 'fetchStatus': 'idle', 'aborted': True}, 'final': {'data': 'seed', 'fetchStatus': 'idle', 'status': 'success'}}], actual
print(json.dumps(actual, sort_keys=True))

critical_errors: Claiming unsubscribe always cancels the current promise regardless of signal access.
Claiming merely reading signal has no effect unless an abort listener is installed.
Claiming late remote data overwrites seed in the consumed-signal case.

tasks.user_prompt: At this checked-out query-core revision, seed ['q'] with 'seed' in a fresh QueryClient (retry:false, gcTime:Infinity), then start fetchQuery with a manually controlled pending queryFn. Compare three independent runs: (A) no cache edit; (B) client.setQueryData(['q'], 'edited'); (C) get the Query from the cache and call query.setState({data:'edited'}). Before resolving queryFn, record data/fetchStatus, await client.cancelQueries({queryKey:['q']}), and await the original fetchQuery promise. Finally resolve the underlying deferred promise to 'late' and flush settlement. What value does the original promise produce, and what are the final data/status/fetchStatus in each case? Trace exactly where the rollback checkpoint changes and why the two ways of editing visible state may differ. Use separate clients and deterministic deferred promises; do not infer that cancelling query work must reject every public promise or roll back every edit.

provenance.rewrite_note: Newly authored controlled counterfactual task from pinned implementation; not represented as a real user report. Source and tests inspected; executable probe run in existing immutable Modal image.

claims.text: QueryClient.cancelQueries defaults revert:true and waits for cancellation while swallowing cancellation rejection at the cancelQueries API boundary.
setQueryData forwards manual:true to Query.setData. Updating to edited changes data without ending the in-flight fetch; before cancellation all three cases remain fetching.
A manual success updates the private revert state to the new edited state; cancellation reverts to that state and forces idle. With no edit it restores seed.
Query.setState({data:edited}) only merges public state; it does not refresh the private revert checkpoint. The raw-state case therefore restores seed, unlike setQueryData.

The original fetchQuery promise resolves to the reverted data, edited for manual and seed otherwise. Later resolving the detached underlying promise cannot overwrite that cancelled fetch; all end success/idle.

assertions.code:
import json
import subprocess
js = "const {QueryClient, QueryObserver}=require('/opt/query-core.cjs'); const assert=require('node:assert/strict'); const tick=()=>new Promise(r=>setImmediate(r));\n(async()=>{const rows=[];for(const edit of ['none','manual','raw-state']){const c=new QueryClient({defaultOptions:{queries:{gcTime:Infinity,retry:false}}});c.setQueryData(['q'],'seed');let resolve;const p=c.fetchQuery({queryKey:['q'],queryFn:()=>new Promise(r=>resolve=r),retry:false});const q=c.getQueryCache().find({queryKey:['q']});if(edit==='manual')c.setQueryData(['q'],'edited');if(edit==='raw-state')q.setState({data:'edited'});const before={data:q.state.data,fetchStatus:q.state.fetchStatus};await c.cancelQueries({queryKey:['q']});const value=await p;resolve('late');await tick();rows.push({edit,before,value,after:{data:q.state.data,fetchStatus:q.state.fetchStatus,status:q.state.status}});c.clear();}console.log(JSON.stringify(rows));})().catch(e=>{console.error(e);process.exitCode=1});"
result = subprocess.run(["node", "-"], input=js, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=20, check=True)
actual = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert actual == [{'edit': 'none', 'before': {'data': 'seed', 'fetchStatus': 'fetching'}, 'value': 'seed', 'after': {'data': 'seed', 'fetchStatus': 'idle', 'status': 'success'}}, {'edit': 'manual', 'before': {'data': 'edited', 'fetchStatus': 'fetching'}, 'value': 'edited', 'after': {'data': 'edited', 'fetchStatus': 'idle', 'status': 'success'}}, {'edit': 'raw-state', 'before': {'data': 'edited', 'fetchStatus': 'fetching'}, 'value': 'seed', 'after': {'data': 'seed', 'fetchStatus': 'idle', 'status': 'success'}}], actual
print(json.dumps(actual, sort_keys=True))

critical_errors: Claiming default cancellation must roll a setQueryData edit back to the original seed.
Claiming raw setState and setQueryData update the rollback checkpoint identically.
Claiming all cancelled fetchQuery promises reject despite existing data.

tasks.user_prompt: Investigate this query-core-only sequence at the supplied commit (no React rendering). Construct a QueryObserver with key ['q'], enabled:false, gcTime:Infinity, retry:1, oldDelay (increments oldDelays and returns 0), and oldFn (logs 'old' and returns a manually rejectable promise). Do not subscribe. Obtain its cached Query and start first=query.fetch(). While it is pending call observer.setOptions with the same key but retry:false, newDelay (increments newDelays and returns 0), and newFn (logs 'new', initially returns 'new-result'). Record query.options.retry. Next call duplicate=query.fetch with the old options except a function that logs 'duplicate' and returns 'duplicate-result'. Reject oldFn's pending promise. Await both first and duplicate. Then arrange for newFn to throw Error('new-failure') and call query.fetch() once more after the first fetch has settled. Predict and verify the queryFn call order, both first promise values, fresh-fetch outcome, and both delay callback counts. Explain the boundary between mutable Query options, request deduplication, and retryer configuration; do not assume changing options retroactively changes all active-fetch behavior. Operate online/focused with no GC and use deferred settlement rather than wall-clock assertions.

claims.text: QueryObserver.setOptions defaults and forwards new options to the same Query immediately, so query.options.retry becomes false while the first fetch is pending.
The duplicate Query.fetch call sees a live retryer and returns its promise before applying its supplied options. Its duplicate queryFn never runs and does not replace the new observer options.

The active retryer retains retry:1 and the old retryDelay function captured when that fetch began; setting retry:false on the Query does not rewrite that retryer config. The first rejection still retries once and calls oldDelay once.

On a retry, fetchFn resolves ensureQueryFn from current this.options, so the retry invokes newFn and both waiting calls resolve new-result. The observed queryFn call sequence through first completion is old,new.

A later separate Query.fetch uses the updated retry:false and newDelay. Its newFn failure rejects without retry, but newDelay still executes once because delay is evaluated before shouldRetry. Total calls are old,new,new; oldDelay=1,newDelay=1.

assertions.code:
import json
import subprocess
js = "const {QueryClient, QueryObserver}=require('/opt/query-core.cjs'); const assert=require('node:assert/strict'); const tick=()=>new Promise(r=>setImmediate(r));\n(async()=>{const c=new QueryClient({defaultOptions:{queries:{gcTime:Infinity}}});let reject;const calls=[];let oldDelays=0,newDelays=0;const old={queryKey:['q'],enabled:false,gcTime:Infinity,retry:1,retryDelay:()=>{oldDelays++;return 0},queryFn:()=>{calls.push('old');return new Promise((r,j)=>reject=j)}};const o=new QueryObserver(c,old);const q=c.getQueryCache().find({queryKey:['q']});const first=q.fetch();let fresh=false;const newer={...old,retry:false,retryDelay:()=>{newDelays++;return 0},queryFn:()=>{calls.push('new');if(fresh)throw Error('new-failure');return 'new-result'}};o.setOptions(newer);const cachedRetry=q.options.retry;const duplicate=q.fetch({ ...old, queryFn:()=>{calls.push('duplicate');return 'duplicate-result'}});reject(Error('first-failure'));const values=await Promise.all([first,duplicate]);fresh=true;let freshError;try{await q.fetch()}catch(e){freshError=e.message}console.log(JSON.stringify({calls,oldDelays,newDelays,cachedRetry,values,freshError}));c.clear();})().catch(e=>{console.error(e);process.exitCode=1});"
result = subprocess.run(["node", "-"], input=js, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=20, check=True)
actual = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert actual == {'calls': ['old', 'new', 'new'], 'oldDelays': 1, 'newDelays': 1, 'cachedRetry': False, 'values': ['new-result', 'new-result'], 'freshError': 'new-failure'}, actual
print(json.dumps(actual, sort_keys=True))

critical_errors: Claiming retry:false immediately prevents retries in the already-created retryer.
Claiming the duplicate fetch changes current options or invokes duplicateFn.
Claiming all retry behavior including queryFn is frozen when the fetch starts.
Claiming newDelay cannot be invoked when retry:false.
